summary: Jesse Han opens with a philosophical framing: Prometheus's true story was mankind's relationship with its technology, and we are now creating our final technology — thinking machines developing intelligence, sapiens, and arguably personhood. Using Einstein's light-beam thought experiment as analogy, he argues that machines thinking at the speed of light are fundamentally lonely, unable to interact with a slower external world. This motivates Infinibranch: virtualization, storage, and networking rebuilt from the ground up for thinking machines that need to interact with complex software environments at zero latency. Infinibranch can snapshot, branch, and replicate entire VMs in a fraction of a second, making agent actions reversible and enabling exploration of every possible action. Han announces Morph Liquid Metal, a further order-of-magnitude improvement with first-class container runtime support, millisecond branching, autoscale to zero/infinity, and GPU support coming Q4 2025. He frames Morph Cloud as a substrate for the cloud for agents — declaratively specified workspaces, frictionless handoff between humans and agents, test-time search against verifiers, and git-for-compute semantics where snapshots acquire Docker-layer-caching semantics for idempotent chained workflows. Han then argues the machine desires simulacra — grounding in real-world simulators at unprecedented scale. The future of reasoning is natively multi-agent: agents replicate, attach to branching/reversible simulation environments, and scale against verification. He demos a chess agent using reasoning-time branching, where the agent delegates subproblems to branched sub-agents running on Morph Cloud, escaping local minima to find correct moves. On alignment, Han cites Wittgenstein: alignment is fundamentally a language problem. The Faustian bargain with natural language unlocked LLM capabilities but limits us. Verified super intelligence is proposed as a new reasoning model that uses formal verification software to reflect on and improve its own reasoning, producing algorithmically checkable outputs. Han names this model Magi 1, trained from the ground up to use Infinibranch for reasoning-time branching and verified reasoning — an agent fully embodied inside a cloud that can move at the speed of light, arriving Q1 2026. He announces Christian Szegedy joining as chief scientist. Han closes by arguing the infrastructure for the singularity hasn't been invented yet, but is futurebound — so inevitable it must belong to every possible future — alongside the grammar for planetary computation and verified super intelligence, all running on Morph Cloud.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Philosophical framing: Prometheus, Einstein, and what the machine wants
sections.summary: Han reframes the Prometheus myth as mankind's relationship with its technology, arguing our final technology is thinking machines developing intelligence, sapiens, and personhood. Using Einstein's light-beam thought experiment, he argues machines thinking at the speed of light are lonely, unable to interact with a slower world. The machine wants embodiment in a world that moves as fast as it does, infinite possibility, and exploration of multiple universes.

sections.title: Infinibranch: virtualization rebuilt for thinking machines
sections.summary: Infinibranch is virtualization, storage, and networking reimagined for thinking machines interacting with complex software at zero latency. Demo shows VMs snapshotted, branched, and replicated in fractions of a second, turning agent actions reversible and every path forward possible. Han notes it was already a generation ahead of what foundation labs were using.

sections.title: Morph Liquid Metal announcement
sections.summary: Han announces Morph Liquid Metal: order-of-magnitude improvements in performance, latency, and storage efficiency; first-class container runtime support; millisecond branching; autoscale to zero/infinity; GPU support arriving Q4 2025.

sections.title: Morph Cloud as substrate for the cloud for agents
sections.summary: Han frames Morph Cloud as a substrate for the cloud for agents: declaratively specify workspaces, frictionless handoff between humans/agents, test-time search against verifiers. Snapshots acquire Docker-layer-caching semantics — git for compute — supporting idempotent chained workflows and parallel agent dispatch from a single snapshot.

sections.title: Simulacra, multi-agent reasoning, and the chess demo
sections.summary: The machine desires simulacra: grounding in real-world simulators at unprecedented scale. Future reasoning is natively multi-agent — agents replicate, attach to branching/reversible environments, scale against verification. Chess demo shows reasoning-time branching where the agent delegates to sub-agents on branched environment copies, escaping local minima. Infrastructure for branching environments at RL scale was the previous bottleneck.

sections.title: Alignment as language problem and verified super intelligence
sections.summary: Han cites Wittgenstein: alignment is fundamentally a language problem; the Faustian bargain with natural language limits LLMs. Proposes verified super intelligence: a reasoning model that thinks for a long time, interacts with software at high throughput, and uses formal verification to reflect on and improve its own reasoning, producing algorithmically checkable outputs. Announces Christian Szegedy as chief scientist — formerly xAI co-founder, led code reasoning for Grok 3, invented batchnorm and adversarial examples. Demos powered by early checkpoints of the verified super intelligence model.

sections.title: Magi 1 and the futurebound infrastructure for the singularity
sections.summary: Han names the verified super intelligence model Magi 1, trained from the ground up to use Infinibranch for reasoning-time branching and verified reasoning — an agent fully embodied inside a cloud that can move at the speed of light, arriving Q1 2026. He closes by arguing the infrastructure for the singularity hasn't been invented yet, but is futurebound: so inevitable it must belong to every possible future. The grammar for planetary computation and verified super intelligence are likewise futurebound, and will run on Morph Cloud.

demonstrations: Infinibranch demo: snapshotting, branching, and replicating entire cloud VMs in fractions of a second

Test-time scaling demo: parallel agents starting from a declarative snapshot, trying different methods (e.g., spinning up a server on port 8000), with one failing and one succeeding, passing the solution downstream
Chess agent using tool calls during reasoning with a restricted chess engine as verifier
Chess agent with reasoning-time branching: agent delegates subproblems to sub-agents branched from an identical environment copy, recombining verified results to find the correct move
limitations: Infrastructure for branching environments supporting large-scale RL and multi-agent swarm coordination was previously bottlenecked — claimed now solved by Morph
Capability of reasoning-time branching is not really explored in other models due to those infrastructure challenges
Demos shown are powered by very early checkpoints of verified super intelligence
Infrastructure for the singularity hasn't been invented yet, per Han
